app.name: Patient Administration System
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: This page says what these pages keep in your browser, and why. What the organisation that runs this system records about you is in its own privacy notice.
privacy.choices.heading: Choices you make
privacy.choices.body: When you choose a theme or a language, your browser remembers it, so that the next page and your next visit look the way you asked. A choice says only which option you picked: it does not identify you.
privacy.theme: Theme (Follow this device, Light or Dark): kept in a cookie named theme and in this browser's local storage, for up to 400 days, and only once you choose. The cookie lets the server send each page in your theme straight away.
privacy.language: Language: kept in a cookie named locale for a year, set when you open a page in a language, so that a link without a language opens in yours.
privacy.signin.heading: Signing in
privacy.signin.session: When you sign in, a cookie holds a random number that links this browser to your session on the server. It holds no name and no password, and it ends when you sign out or after a time without use.
privacy.signin.tx: While you sign in, a second cookie, for up to 10 minutes, checks that the answer from the sign-in service belongs to the sign-in you started.
privacy.none: These pages set no advertising or analytics cookies, do not follow you to other sites, and share none of this with anyone.
privacy.remove.heading: Removing them
privacy.remove.body: Signing out ends the sign-in cookie. To forget your theme and language, clear this site's data in your browser's settings; the pages then follow your device and your browser's language again.

tol.title: Tolerances: red, amber, green
tol.intro: How far each measure may drift from its target. Green is within the tolerance. Amber is past it but within the limit. Red is past the limit and needs someone to act. A measure with no data is never shown as green. For percentages, the tolerance and limit are in percentage points.

tol.alerts.title: Alerts
tol.alerts.intro: A measure that goes past its red limit opens an alert. It closes by itself when the measure is no longer red. Acknowledging an alert says someone is looking at it; it does not close it.
